The corrected probe preserves the original decision test: complete IK coverage would rule out workspace impossibility, while compiled inertial quantities and reset/representative action responses determine whether the first learning direction should prioritize transient capture, braking and hold regulation, or official inner-radius coverage.

request.description: Train a fresh PPO policy on the full official target-radius range while retaining the existing observation, action interface, reward, and network recipe.
request.rationale: M5 measured complete constrained-IK reachability across the sampled official annulus and showed that impulse responses settle within roughly 7 to 9 control steps, so the leading actionable uncertainty is not geometric impossibility but whether learning covers the omitted inner-radius band while producing a stable uninterrupted hold. The prior training range excluded 0.06 to 0.14 m despite official evaluation including it. This run directly tests the coverage explanation under the full 120000-step allocation; its checkpoints can then be evaluated with hold-specific diagnostics. A poor result concentrated in inner radii would support further curriculum or representation work, while broad success would shift attention to residual hold robustness and temporal observability.

request.description: Evaluate the strongest non-terminal and terminal checkpoints from T1 on the same 160-episode development panel, including complete-hold outcomes and radius/angle, first-reach, minimum-distance, hold-length, and interruption diagnostics.
request.rationale: T1 training success rose from zero to 0.58 after expanding training to the official radius range, but training statistics do not establish complete uninterrupted hold performance. The unresolved distinction is whether the learned behavior truly satisfies the hold or merely optimizes apparent reach/reward. Comparing T1:checkpoint-115712 with T1:checkpoint-120832 on identical seeds tests whether the terminal checkpoint is genuinely stronger and whether failures are concentrated in inner radii, late capture, or hold interruptions. Strong complete-hold performance across the radius range supports continuing the current route; high reach with short or interrupted holds redirects toward regulation and temporal-state methods; inner-radius failures redirect toward coverage or representation changes.

request.candidates_and_roles: No formal model role has been assigned. T1:checkpoint-120832 is the strongest evidence-backed development candidate at 93.75% on M6; T1:checkpoint-115712 is the matched non-terminal reference at 88.75%. Neither meets the human goal or has official assessment evidence.
request.cumulative_resource_use: M5 used one completed PI-owned dynamics measurement. T1 used one fresh training run with 120000 requested steps and 120832 completed rollout steps. M6 used two 160-episode research evaluations on the same development seeds, for 320 evaluation episodes total. No official assessment or additional training allocation has been used.
request.current_goal_gap: The best measured development result is 150/160 successes (93.75%), leaving 10 failures and a 4.25 percentage-point gap to the 98% target. Official 200-episode assessment has not been requested. The available evidence does not yet identify whether the gap is dominated by hold interruptions, late capture, inner-radius geometry, target angle, or branch/transient behavior.
request.current_synthesis: Observed: M5 found at least one joint-limit-feasible IK branch for all 576 sampled official radius-angle combinations, while the open and folded branches were individually feasible for 84.375% and 85.764% of samples. M5 also measured substantial action-induced endpoint motion and settling within approximately 7-9 control steps in the tested configurations, with the reset Jacobian singular and non-singular representative configurations better conditioned. Interpretation: workspace impossibility is not the leading explanation for the remaining goal gap, and the plant has enough passive settling that a learned state-feedback controller can plausibly solve the task, although the probe is not a policy-level hold test. Observed: T1 training on the full official radius range produced checkpoints whose training success rose to 0.58, but training statistics are not development evidence. Observed: matched-seed M6 evaluation gave 142/160 successes (88.75%) for checkpoint-115712 and 150/160 (93.75%) for checkpoint-120832; the terminal checkpoint won 10 shared episodes versus 2 for the reference, with 12 discordant episodes. Interpretation: continued optimization under the full-radius recipe improves measured complete-hold performance, so the route is supported, but the terminal candidate remains below the human goal. Limit: the current record exposes aggregate success and the existence of per-episode diagnostics, not an interpreted breakdown of the ten failures by radius, angle, first reach, hold length, or interruption.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved scientific distinction is whether the residual 6.25% development failure rate is primarily (a) a local regulation failure in which policies enter tolerance but lose the uninterrupted 100-step hold through boundary margin, residual velocity, or oscillation, (b) a capture-time failure caused by the reset singularity or late convergence, or (c) a geometry-generalization failure concentrated in inner radii, target angles, or branch-dependent transients. These explanations imply different next interventions: regulation failures call for hold-aware control or reward/interface changes; capture failures call for transient/trajectory changes; geometry concentration calls for targeted coverage or representation changes. Episode diagnostics from matched evaluations, binned by target geometry and hold trajectory, discriminate them. If failures are predominantly interrupted holds after first reach, change direction toward stabilization; if they are predominantly late or never reaching specific geometry bins, change toward capture or coverage; if no class dominates, retain the full-radius route and test policy variance/temporal observability.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal is at least 98% complete uninterrupted-hold episode success under the official 0.06-0.20 m target distribution. The completed development evaluation establishes a strong but insufficient candidate at 93.75%, so the campaign must preserve and improve complete-hold behavior rather than optimize reward or first reach alone.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Checkpoint the startup synthesis and carry the failure-mechanism question into goal review. Continue the full-radius learning route provisionally because M6 improved over the earlier checkpoint and M5 ruled out broad workspace infeasibility, but do not request official assessment. The next scientific action should interpret the recorded per-episode hold and geometry diagnostics before changing the policy, reward, or training distribution.
request.next_question: Among the ten failures of T1:checkpoint-120832 on the matched 160-episode development panel, are failures primarily complete-hold interruptions after first entry, late or absent capture, or concentration in specific target-radius/angle or IK-branch regions, and which failure mechanism should determine the next intervention toward 98% official success?

request.closure_condition: Close when completed evidence classifies the ten terminal-candidate failures by first entry, hold interruption, target radius and angle, and IK-branch behavior well enough to select or reject a capture, stabilization, or geometry/representation intervention; if no class dominates, record the mixed result and the next discriminating method.

request.rationale: M5 ruled out broad workspace impossibility and showed that the plant can settle, while M6 established that the terminal candidate reaches 93.75% but did not interpret its diagnostics. Direct reading of the M6 artifact shows seven failures with no recorded tolerance entry, one first entry at step 116, and two early entries followed by short holds, so late or absent capture currently appears more prevalent than post-entry interruption. The failures also appear concentrated in particular angle sectors and span both inner and outer radii, but the artifact does not expose IK-branch behavior. This inquiry will distinguish a recipe-specific capture/geometry deficit from a local hold-regulation deficit before changing the learning route.
